title: SanPiN in 2026: what changed and what stayed the same
excerpt: From 1 September 2026, SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26 replaces 3590-20: numbering changes, requirements stay the same. Here is what to know about logs, retention periods, and Article 6.6 fines of the Russian Code of Administrative Offences.

body.text: From 1 September 2026, the main food-service regulation is SanPiN 2.3/2.4.4282-26, which replaces 2.3/2.4.3590-20. The clause numbering has changed, but the foundation is the same as it has been since 2021. Here is what you need to keep in mind now.

items: Employee health log (hygiene log) — every shift, for every employee.
Finished-product rejection log — for every batch.
Refrigeration-equipment temperature log — at least twice a day.
Incoming raw-material inspection — at every delivery.
Disinfectant-use log — each time disinfectant is used.

body.text: The minimum retention period is 12 months. For records connected with HACCP (audits, CAPA, traceability), it is 3 years. If food poisoning is suspected, records for the most recent 12 months are examined first, so they must not be lost.

body.title: Important
body.text: Under Article 6.6 of the Russian Code of Administrative Offences, fines can reach RUB 30,000 for an official and RUB 100,000 for a legal entity. Failing to keep a required log is treated the same as violating the underlying requirement.

items: The responsible person’s signature is missing: an approval or suspension is recorded without a name.
A shift is missing: Monday’s entry is there, Tuesday’s is not.
Temperatures are suspiciously identical: +4, +4, +4, +4. An inspector can spot falsification in seconds.
A batch is not linked to its delivery note: the rejection record lacks supplier details.

body.text: Automation is used where it is safe: work schedules, job roles, and standard products. Where a real measurement is needed—temperature or product rejection—automatic filling is disabled, and the log cannot be closed without an actual value.
